name: Stinson L-5 Sentinel
summary: Standard US Army liaison airplane of WWII, the 'Flying Jeep', with tandem seats, big flaps and a Lycoming six; many were sold surplus and fly as private warbirds.

wings: High, strut-braced wing with large drooping flaps
Slotted flaps and wide-chord, rounded tips
engines: Single six-cylinder flat engine in a smooth rounded cowl
fuselage: Tandem seats under a long glazed cabin with an enormous rear window and skylight
Long, slender rear fuselage that tapers to the tail
Long-travel main gear on a tailwheel airplane
tail: Rounded fin and rudder with a balanced horn
Horizontal tail strut-braced to the fuselage

tellTales: Tandem high-wing with a long, heavily glazed cabin and a huge rear window
Smooth rounded cowl and slender, tapering fuselage with a braced tail
Huge flaps that droop steeply on the strut-braced wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The Bird Dog has a squarer, taller tail and spring-steel gear legs; the L-5 has a rounder tail and a smoother, curvier fuselage.
The Cub has a tiny rectangular cabin and a small four-cylinder nose; the L-5 is larger with a long glazed greenhouse and a six-cylinder cowl.
The L-3 is much smaller with a stubby nose; the L-5 is bigger with a longer cowl and a sloping glazed rear.
The Stinson 108 is a four-seat civilian derivative with a bigger cabin and two rows of side seats; the L-5 is a tandem two-seater.
